value.body: A fashion designer creates clothing or accessory designs and turns them into collections that can be produced and sold. Apparel brands, export houses, retail chains and designer labels hire them. Day-to-day work includes trend research, sketching, preparing technical specifications and checking samples with the production team.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Des in Fashion, Textile or Accessory Design

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Sketching, design software, pattern and tech-pack templates

items.label: Fashion technology UG students
items.note: Undergraduate enrolment in this subject; fashion design is also taught under B.Des
items.source: AISHE 2023-24 (Ministry of Education), institutions that reported

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually start as an assistant or junior designer at a brand, an export house or with an established designer, often through a graduation-project showcase or internship. Some launch their own label later, after gaining production experience.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: designer, senior designer, design manager, or merchandising roles.
Early roles often involve long hours around collection and sampling deadlines.
Starting an own label needs business, sourcing and marketing skills as well as design.
